scene_summary: A small office with a blind-covered window, cubby shelf, floor lamp, two rolling chairs, tables, and a potted plant.
overall_evidence: The reconstruction captures the principal furniture types and their broad arrangement, but the viewpoint is much wider and more elevated, the prominent paneled door is not visibly reproduced, and the flooring, table surfaces, and room enclosure look substantially different.

main_defects.description: The reconstruction uses a much wider, higher, pulled-back view, exposing the room's open edges and a large empty floor area rather than filling the frame with the interior.
main_defects.evidence: The reference is a close interior view with walls extending beyond the frame; the reconstruction shows wall tops, exterior gray background, and much smaller furniture in the frame.
main_defects.uncertainty: The different view also affects apparent object sizes and visibility, so some layout differences cannot be attributed confidently to geometry alone.

main_defects.description: The large dark paneled door on the right side of the reference is not visibly recognizable in the reconstruction.
main_defects.evidence: The reference has a large dark door with eight inset panels; the reconstruction shows a narrow gray edge and white side wall instead of a comparable door face.
main_defects.uncertainty: A door could be hidden or seen edge-on because of the changed viewpoint.

main_defects.description: The reference's dark, varied brown wood floor and dark gray table surfaces are much lighter and flatter in the reconstruction.
main_defects.evidence: The reconstructed floor consists of pale, fairly uniform rectangular planks, and the visible tabletop is nearly white; the reference floor has visibly darker wood grain and the tabletop is charcoal gray.
main_defects.uncertainty: Lighting and exposure may contribute to the color difference.

main_defects.description: The chairs and tables have a different apparent arrangement: the reconstructed chairs sit farther back relative to the tables, and the separate foreground table surface is prominently detached.
main_defects.evidence: In the reference both chairs occupy the central floor alongside the large foreground desk; in the reconstruction the left chair is tucked directly against the shelf, while a second rectangular surface lies distinctly in front of the main table.
main_defects.uncertainty: Perspective, framing, and occlusion make the actual spacing and whether the foreground surface connects to the table uncertain.

main_defects.description: The window and shelf appear much smaller relative to the visible wall and furniture in the reconstruction.
main_defects.evidence: The reference blind is a dominant broad feature above a wide shelf; in the reconstruction the blind and shelf occupy a compact area on a much larger exposed wall.
main_defects.uncertainty: The pulled-back camera accounts for some apparent size difference, so a true dimensional mismatch is not certain.

strengths: The window blind and light wood cubby shelf are placed together on the same wall.
Two light-colored rolling chairs, a slender floor lamp, white cabinet, tables, and a spiky plant are all recognizable.
The room retains light walls, a plank-pattern floor, and a generally similar office furniture grouping.
uncertainty: This is an initial automated visual judgment from two images, not a human rating or validated metric. Different camera position, field of view, lighting, and occlusion complicate judgments about dimensions, placement, and unseen objects. No hidden geometry has been assessed.
